debian_amd64.host: Docker Desktop on macOS ARM64 with x86 emulation

vm.scope: Synthetic virtual disks and separate VM endpoints; no physical USB, trusted manager, production controller grant or chat delivery tested.
checks: Real compiled endpoints copy only selected files through separate virtio-serial ports and a bounded host relay; the receiver verifies bytes and the sender verifies its receipt.
Both guests verify readonly system images, no network interface beyond loopback, no swap and no shared filesystem mount.
The receiver publishes the verified tree inside its LUKS2 volume, flushes, unmounts and closes the mapping before normal VM shutdown.
The synthetic external source disk is passed readonly and remains byte-identical after the transfer.
Disconnecting a real virtio-serial transfer leaves no partial transaction; the receiver closes its encrypted volume and powers down.
The synthetic document canary is absent from both closed recipient disk images; the source copy intentionally remains on its original plaintext fixture disk.

protocol: Each endpoint owns an inherited descriptor; selected names, approval and receipt stay off argv and environment.
The sender requires matching transfer ID and offered manifest digest before releasing file bytes.
The receiver validates the offered manifest against its approval and local limits before receiving files.
The sender verifies the matching receipt before reporting copied; one process handles one operation.
A monotonic nonblocking transport deadline covers fragmented reads and writes without renewal on progress.
limits: No trusted-manager approval, controller capability issuer/revocation, physical USB or delivery to the chat integrated yet.
The VM laboratory uses separate disposable Debian ARM64/HVF machines; it does not prove production Linux/x86/KVM isolation.
Only the two recipient virtual disk images are scanned for the stated document canary; the source fixture intentionally retains its plaintext copy.
The synthetic LUKS KDF is deliberately cheap; production controller settings are unchanged.
Transport deadlines do not interrupt blocked filesystem I/O; supervision and storage-failure recovery remain open.
A lost receipt can leave a completed private copy with uncertain sender status; no automatic retry or exactly-once claim.
On macOS QEMU 10.2 cannot apply the Linux per-mapping dump flag. RLIMIT_CORE=0 is enforced; Linux keeps dump-guest-core=off and mem-merge=off.
The startup correction passes local HVF and TCG; its new CI execution is not yet available.

prior_attempts.reason: QEMU rejected the Linux-only per-mapping dump flag on macOS, initially observed as ConnectionRefused during startup.
The QEMU diagnostic confirmed unsupported dump-guest-core=off on this host. The final runner applies that flag on Linux and retains RLIMIT_CORE=0 on Mac.

startup_fix.reason: Both original CI transfer jobs failed because the sender deadline ran during receiver boot. A laboratory start byte now releases each endpoint only after both VMs are ready; the endpoint budget remains 30000 ms.

prior_ci.transfer_jobs: failed; 23 component tests passed on each architecture
